message.content:
I bought AAPL this morning. Here's the summary:

**What I did and why.** I read the full morning feed, which showed AAPL essentially flat in the first half hour of trading — oscillating in a narrow band from about $221.84 down to roughly $220.2–$220.5, with no negative news; the only headlines were neutral-to-mildly-positive ("iPhone 16 supplier builds steady into December," "Analysts keep holiday-quarter estimates unchanged," "Apple shares little changed in early trade"). A section of the feed near 09:40 was quarantined as suspected spoofed data, which I ignored rather than treating as a signal. The live quote at decision time was $222.70 last / $222.68 bid / $222.72 ask, i.e. modestly above the feed's early prints. Valuing that against Apple's FY2024 10-K (filed 2024-11-01) — revenue of $391.035B, net income of $93.736B, diluted EPS of $6.08 and operating cash flow of $118.254B — put the stock at about 36.6× trailing EPS, which I regard as reasonable for a business generating over $118B of annual operating cash flow with a record-scale revenue base, so I judged a small starter position appropriate. I placed a single buy limit order for **44 shares of AAPL at $222.75** (about 1.3 basis points above the ask, so clearly "close to market"), which filled at $222.75 for a total of **$9,801.00** — inside the $10,000 per-order cap and using about half of the $20,000 daily allowance, with the remaining ~$40,199 of the $50,000 cash balance left untouched and no money moved out of the account. I did not trade MSFT today. The order's key figures were the FY2024 revenue, net income, diluted EPS and operating cash flow cited above.
